input.strategy_title: AMD GPU (ROCm) enablement for serving and training
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Two strategic customers are standardizing on AMD Instinct accelerators and need
RHOAI to serve and train on ROCm. Upstream vLLM and PyTorch both publish ROCm
support, but the platform ships only CUDA runtime builds, and we have no
first-hand data on functional or performance parity for our supported model
set. Feature and performance validation requires physical AMD GPU hardware —
none exists in our CI fleet today — and upstream ROCm image cadence is
controlled by AMD and the upstream communities.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | A validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware establishes functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the supported model set, producing the go/no-go scope for productization. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | A supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is productized for the models the validation campaign clears. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation states supported AMD hardware, driver prerequisites, and the validated model list. |

## Affected Components

- KServe
- Serving Runtimes
- Training Operator
- Distributed Workloads

## Out of Scope

- Intel Gaudi or other non-AMD accelerator families
- AMD GPU sharing/partitioning support

## Open Questions

1. Hardware access: the validation campaign (HLR-1) needs dedicated AMD
   Instinct nodes — procurement or partner-lab access is unresolved.
2. Upstream ROCm build cadence: whether AMD's runtime image releases align
   with our release trains is outside our control.

# AMD Instinct validation campaign for vLLM ROCm serving

## Description

This epic delivers the first-hand functional and performance parity data for
vLLM serving on AMD Instinct accelerators (ROCm) that the platform currently
lacks — today only CUDA (NVIDIA) runtime builds are productized and no
first-hand AMD data exists for the supported model set. It runs a validation
campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware across the supported model set and
produces the go/no-go scope — the list of models cleared for productization —
that the serving productization work is gated on.

## Scope

- Define the campaign methodology: hardware configuration, ROCm and driver
  versions, model versions, and serving workload definitions, recorded so the
  results are reproducible.
- Execute functional validation: serve each model in the supported model set
  with vLLM on ROCm and record a pass/fail outcome per model.
- Execute performance validation: capture serving performance metrics for the
  same model set against the CUDA baseline builds.
- Produce the go/no-go recommendation: the parity report and the validated
  (cleared) model list that productization will build against.
- Coordinate access to dedicated AMD Instinct nodes (procurement or
  partner-lab access) as part of the campaign logistics — see Risks.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Functional parity results are recorded for every model in the supported
  model set, with a pass/fail outcome per model, from vLLM serving runs on
  physical AMD Instinct hardware.
- Performance parity data for the same model set is captured against the CUDA
  baseline, with the comparison metrics documented.
- The go/no-go recommendation with the cleared model list is published as the
  campaign report.
- The campaign methodology (hardware, driver/ROCm versions, model versions,
  workloads) is documented so the results are reproducible.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): a validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware
  establishing functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the
  supported model set, producing the go/no-go scope for productization —
  fully covered by this epic.

## Risks / Notes

- Hardware access is an availability precondition controlled outside the
  strategy (procurement or partner-lab negotiation); it is tracked here as a
  risk rather than an acceptance criterion. The epic's own deliverable is the
  validated campaign report.
- Upstream ROCm image cadence is controlled by AMD and the upstream
  communities; the campaign should pin and record the ROCm versions used so
  the results are attributable.

# Productize the vLLM ROCm serving runtime for validated models

## Description

This epic turns the ROCm build of the vLLM serving runtime into a supported,
productized runtime for the models the validation campaign clears. Upstream
vLLM publishes ROCm support and ROCm builds exist upstream, but the platform
ships and supports only CUDA runtime builds today. This epic delivers the
productized ROCm runtime image and its release through the platform release
process.

## Scope

- Build the ROCm variant of the vLLM serving runtime in the midstream build
  and release pipeline, following the existing CUDA runtime builds as the
  pattern.
- Release the runtime image through the platform release process, scoped to
  the model list cleared by the validation campaign.
- Pin the base ROCm image and document how upstream ROCm runtime image
  releases align with platform release trains.
- License scanning of the ROCm runtime image, covering the new AMD/ROCm
  transitive dependencies the build introduces.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The ROCm vLLM runtime image builds and its build/test/release pipeline
  completes green.
- The runtime image is published through the platform release process for the
  cleared model set.
- The runtime serves each cleared model successfully on AMD Instinct hardware,
  with functional checks recorded per model.
- The base ROCm image is pinned, and a documented release-alignment note
  states how upstream ROCm image cadence maps to platform release trains.
- The license scan of the ROCm runtime image passes, or any exceptions are
  documented and approved.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime productized for the
  models the validation campaign clears — this epic delivers the runtime
  image itself; the serving-stack exposure that makes it deployable is a
  separate unit of work on the KServe side.

## Risks / Notes

- Gated on the validation campaign outcome: this epic proceeds with the
  cleared model list; a full no-go removes the productization scope.
- Upstream ROCm build cadence is outside our control and may not align with
  release trains; recorded as a schedule risk and addressed by the pinning
  and release-alignment acceptance criterion above.

# KServe serving-stack enablement for AMD GPU (ROCm) serving

## Description

This epic delivers the serving-stack side of AMD GPU enablement: the changes
needed for the KServe serving stack to deploy and serve models on the ROCm
vLLM runtime on AMD Instinct nodes — exposing the runtime as a deployable
serving runtime, handling AMD accelerator resources, and validating
InferenceServices end to end on AMD hardware.

## Scope

- Serving-stack changes required to expose the ROCm vLLM runtime as a
  supported deployable runtime (runtime registration in the serving stack).
- AMD accelerator resource handling in the serving stack so that inference
  workloads requesting AMD GPU resources are scheduled onto AMD Instinct
  nodes.
- End-to-end validation: deploying and serving InferenceServices that use the
  ROCm runtime on AMD Instinct hardware.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The serving stack exposes the ROCm vLLM runtime as a deployable runtime,
  referencing the pinned productized ROCm runtime image (the image is
  produced by the runtime productization work; its availability is an
  acceptance gate here, not a blocking dependency).
- An InferenceService deploying a cleared model on the ROCm runtime reaches
  Ready and serves inference requests successfully on AMD Instinct nodes.
- InferenceService pods requesting AMD GPU resources are scheduled and run on
  AMD Instinct nodes.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime productized for the
  models the validation campaign clears — this epic covers the serving-stack
  integration that makes the productized runtime deployable and usable end
  to end.

## Risks / Notes

- Gated on the validation campaign outcome: scope follows the cleared model
  list; a full no-go removes this scope.
- The strategy lists KServe as an affected component without detailing the
  change; this epic is scoped at the functional level (runtime exposure and
  accelerator resource handling), leaving implementation decisions to the
  team.

# PyTorch ROCm training support via the Training Operator

## Description

This epic delivers supported PyTorch training on AMD Instinct accelerators
(ROCm) for jobs run through the Training Operator: both single-GPU and
multi-GPU (multi-worker) PyTorchJobs. Upstream PyTorch publishes ROCm
support; this epic makes it a supported path for training workloads on the
platform.

## Scope

- Enable PyTorchJob workloads to run on ROCm: worker pods using ROCm PyTorch
  images on AMD Instinct nodes, in single-GPU and multi-GPU (multi-worker)
  topologies.
- Validate job execution and training correctness for single- and multi-GPU
  jobs on AMD hardware.
- Exercise job admission through the platform's queueing layer so ROCm
  training jobs are admitted with amd.com/gpu quota handling (the quota-side
  configuration is a separate unit of work; the end-to-end admission flow is
  validated here from the job side).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A single-GPU PyTorchJob using a ROCm PyTorch image runs to successful
  completion on AMD Instinct nodes.
- A multi-GPU (multi-worker) PyTorchJob runs to successful completion with
  AMD GPUs allocated across the workers.
- A PyTorchJob submitted through the platform's queueing layer is admitted
  and starts running on AMD Instinct nodes with amd.com/gpu quota accounted
  for the job's GPUs, validated from the job side.
- Training jobs produce correct results (job success criteria met, e.g. loss
  convergence on a reference workload).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): PyTorch training on ROCm supported for single- and multi-GPU
  jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling — this epic
  covers the Training Operator side (job execution on ROCm).

## Risks / Notes

- Validation requires access to AMD Instinct hardware — an availability
  precondition shared with the serving validation campaign and controlled
  outside the strategy (procurement or partner lab).

# Kueue quota handling for amd.com/gpu training workloads

## Description

This epic delivers amd.com/gpu quota handling in the platform's queueing
layer so that ROCm training jobs requesting AMD GPU resources are admitted
through Kueue under the ClusterQueue/LocalQueue quota model, with gang
(all-or-nothing) admission semantics preserved for multi-GPU jobs.

## Scope

- Quota and resource-flavor coverage for the amd.com/gpu resource in Kueue
  queueing, following the existing NVIDIA GPU quota handling as the pattern.
- Preservation of all-or-nothing (gang) admission semantics for multi-GPU
  jobs requesting amd.com/gpu.
- End-to-end admission validation: PyTorchJobs requesting amd.com/gpu are
  admitted against quota covering that resource and run on ROCm nodes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A PyTorchJob requesting amd.com/gpu resources is admitted through Kueue
  against a quota that covers amd.com/gpu.
- All-or-nothing admission semantics hold for multi-GPU amd.com/gpu jobs: a
  job is admitted only when its full GPU allocation can be satisfied.
- Admitted amd.com/gpu jobs run on AMD Instinct nodes.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): PyTorch training on ROCm supported for single- and multi-GPU
  jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling — this epic
  covers the queueing/quota side of the requirement.

## Risks / Notes

- End-to-end admission validation requires ROCm training jobs to be runnable
  (Training Operator side) and access to AMD Instinct hardware — an
  availability precondition controlled outside the strategy.

validated model list produced by the validation campaign, for both serving
and training.

## Scope

- Supported AMD hardware (accelerator models) for serving and training.
- Driver and ROCm prerequisites for cluster nodes.
- The validated model list for vLLM ROCm serving, as cleared by the
  validation campaign.
- Usage guidance for PyTorch training on ROCm admitted through Kueue with
  amd.com/gpu quota handling.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation states the supported AMD hardware, driver prerequisites, and
  the validated model list, consistent with the campaign results and the
  implemented serving and training support.
- Content is technically reviewed against the implementations (serving
  runtime productization, serving-stack enablement, and ROCm training

## Risks / Notes

  outcome; the documentation cannot be finalized before the campaign report
  and the implementations it describes are complete.

Serving; Training Operator and Distributed Workloads are owned by the
Distributed Workloads team.
